title: But what about the roads?
description: Section six. Every reader who reaches the end of this page raises the same objection: the government builds the roads. Groups order the page. Every item names its own group and its own card kind. A comparison must be like for like: the same unit, the same year, the same country. Where it is not, say so in the note. A comparison that cannot be sourced on both sides is dropped, not shaded.

lede.description: The paragraph above the groups. Supports the {transportShare} token, which prints the transport slice of outlays.json as a percentage.

caveat.description: Printed under the last group, in the hint style. The honest limits of every comparison above it. This is not optional decoration; the section is dishonest without it.

groups.description: Rendered in this order. An item points at one of these by id.

group.description: The id of a group above. Validation refuses a group that does not exist.

kind.description: multiple: one unit bought twice, the card prints how many times more the public price was. record: one figure that stands on its own, with no arithmetic. reader: worked out in code from the reader's own tax.

label.description: The line under the figure. On a multiple card it reads straight after the ratio, so it starts lower case and names the unit: "more, per kilogram carried to low Earth orbit".

publicPrice.description: Multiple cards only. Dollars the state pays for one unit. Record the year in the note; a programme cost moves when the plan is revised, not on a schedule.

privatePrice.description: Multiple cards only. Dollars a market actor charges for the same one unit. Must be below publicPrice. A card reading "0.8× more" contradicts its own heading, and validation refuses it.

figure.description: Record cards only. Printed exactly as written: "373,000", "1.82%", "10,000 miles". No arithmetic is applied to it.

compute.description: Reader cards only. Names a function in src/lib/render.ts. Add the case there before adding a value here.

sameness.description: Multiple cards only, and required on every one. ONE SENTENCE naming what makes the two sides the same job: same statute, same unit, same buyer, same beat, same year. It is printed first, ahead of the prices. A card that fails to earn this sentence is a card whose critic answers "exactly, it is not the same job" and wins. If you cannot write it, find a narrower unit where the jobs really are identical, or drop the card. Say what makes the sides ALIKE here; the note below is where differences go.

note.description: Shown under the sameness sentence. A multiple card must use both the {public} and {private} tokens, so a reader can divide them and get the ratio back. Name any remaining way in which the two sides are not alike, and name the year of each figure.

source.description: Record and reader cards. Who published the figure.

publicSource.description: Multiple cards. Who published the government price. Prefer an inspector general, an auditor, or the agency's own plan over a news report.

privateSource.description: Multiple cards. Who published the market price. Prefer a published price list over an estimate.
